scope: Primary sources motivate mechanisms. All added address, interface geometry and mismatch controls are explicit teaching assumptions. Existing atlas numeric models remain authoritative for stack and workload totals.

sources.title: Samsung Develops Industry-First 36GB HBM3E 12H DRAM
sources.supports: A named HBM implementation uses thermocompression with non-conductive film; bumps and supporting material have distinct roles.
sources.excludes: The atlas does not reproduce Samsung geometry, process conditions, yield, thermal results or product qualification.

sources.title: SK hynix: Small Size, Big Impact
sources.supports: Mass reflow forms interconnects and molded underfill occupies the inter-die region; these are separate material and process roles.
sources.excludes: No vendor throughput, alloy composition, pad dimensions or route superiority is inferred. The atlas remains a material-role illustration.

sources.title: imec: Wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding — pushing the boundaries to 400nm interconnect pitch
sources.locator: February 19, 2024; Current process flow and Accurate control of surface topography sections
sources.supports: Hybrid bonding combines prepared dielectric surfaces and copper interconnects; surface preparation and registration matter.
sources.excludes: The reported research test vehicle is not a qualified HBM product. Atlas pad width, exaggerated local gap and acceptance offsets are synthetic; overlap does not determine resistance, yield or lifetime.

sources.title: Micron HBM3E product information
sources.locator: FAQ: difference between HBM2 and HBM3E
sources.supports: HBM devices expose a channel and pseudo-channel hierarchy; Micron describes 16 channels and 32 pseudo-channels for HBM3E.
sources.excludes: The atlas two-channel-slices-per-die teaching map, word width, bank counts, rows, columns and address order are not Micron specifications. Existing model dimensions and bandwidths are not replaced with product claims.

sources.title: Intel HBM2 Interface FPGA IP User Guide, UG-20031
sources.locator: 2018.12.24 edition; printed page 21, Address reordering and auto-precharge policy
sources.supports: Controller configuration maps system-side addresses into memory address fields and can change that ordering. Locality and page-hit behavior depend on policy.
sources.excludes: This source is HBM2 controller documentation. Its address widths and protocol modes are not copied into the synthetic map; the explorer is not an AXI/HBM controller or hardware simulator.

sources.title: Microchip: Optimized Access Functionality
sources.supports: Access depends on bank and open-row state. A conflicting row requires precharge and activation before a read; access scheduling can overlap work across banks.
sources.excludes: Only command ordering is illustrated. DDR timings, HBM timing compliance, arbitration, refresh, bank groups and PHY operation are not modeled.

sources.title: NASA/JPL EEE Parts Bulletin: CGA Assemblies under Thermal Cycling
sources.locator: June/July 2013, Volume 5 Issue 3; Equation 1 on printed page 2, discussion on pages 3–4
sources.supports: Differential thermal expansion depends on CTE mismatch, temperature excursion and distance from a neutral point. Dividing free displacement by joint height gives a global geometric shear indicator. Workmanship, use conditions and qualification require separate evidence.
sources.excludes: The source concerns CGA/package-board assemblies, not qualified HBM bonds. Its relationship is used only as an unconstrained teaching analogy for solder-bearing routes, never as calibrated local strain, stress, fatigue life or hybrid-bond mechanics.

sources.title: Kwon et al.: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
sources.locator: SOSP 2023 paper, abstract and memory-management motivation
sources.supports: KV cache grows dynamically and its placement/management affects serving capacity.
sources.excludes: The existing atlas uses aggregate byte accounting, not PagedAttention allocation, paging, fragmentation or benchmark results. The contiguous tier layout is an explicit illustration.

sources.title: Sandisk: Scaling the Memory Wall — Behind High Bandwidth Flash for AI Inferencing
sources.locator: August 6, 2025; What is HBF?, Scaling beyond the memory wall, and disclosure 1
sources.supports: HBF is NAND-based and the cited performance exploration focuses on reading pretrained weights.
sources.excludes: The atlas read-only HBF policy is a teaching allocation choice, not a claim that flash cannot be programmed. Vendor simulated speedups, sample dates, capacity and bandwidth claims do not replace atlas parameters or establish current product availability.
